name: Nikolai Zelinsky
text: His activated-charcoal gas-mask work helped protect soldiers in the First World War. He did not seek a personal patent on the charcoal-filter method.

name: Jagadish Chandra Bose
text: He generally preferred to share his radio discoveries. The familiar claim that he never patented anything needs a correction: a US detector patent was granted in his name in 1904.

name: Alberto Santos-Dumont
text: He made the Demoiselle blueprints freely available so other builders could use them. Detailed construction drawings appeared in print in 1910.

name: Alexander Popov
text: His 1895 receiver demonstration became a landmark in radio history. His contribution belongs alongside the other researchers who made wireless communication possible.

name: Ludwik Zamenhof
text: He offered Esperanto as a language people could learn, use and develop together, rather than as a private monopoly. A shared language was his practical proposal for understanding across borders.

name: Valentin Voyno-Yasenetsky
text: The surgeon and archbishop donated 130,000 rubles of his 200,000-ruble Stalin Prize to children’s homes. A large gift deserves remembering accurately.

name: Chester Carlson
text: Xerography made him wealthy. He gave large sums to educational, humanitarian and other charitable causes, often quietly, and directed much of his fortune toward philanthropy.

name: Jonas Salk
text: The inactivated polio vaccine was not patented, and Salk did not profit from sharing its formulation and production processes. Asked about ownership, he famously asked, “Could you patent the sun?”

name: Frederick Banting, Charles Best and James Collip
russian: ФРЕДЕРИК БАНТИНГ · ЧАРЛЬЗ БЕСТ · ДЖЕЙМС КОЛЛИП
text: In 1923, the insulin patent rights were assigned to the University of Toronto for a symbolic dollar each, intended to protect the discovery from monopoly. This did not itself guarantee permanent affordable access.

name: Wilhelm Röntgen
text: He declined to patent his X-ray apparatus and donated his Nobel Prize money to the University of Würzburg. His discovery could spread without a patent controlled by him.

name: Marie and Pierre Curie
text: The Curies published their radium-isolation processes without patenting them, and supplied other researchers with preparations and practical descriptions.

name: Tim Berners-Lee and CERN
text: Berners-Lee’s invention became a worldwide platform. On April 30, 1993, CERN released key World Wide Web software into the public domain, enabling others to use and build on it freely.

name: Nils Bohlin and Volvo
text: Volvo allowed other manufacturers to use Bohlin’s three-point safety-belt design without a license fee. A patented invention could still be shared to protect people everywhere.
